failure_reason: SAP Commerce/Spartacus storefront; server-rendered SEO shell loads fine (no HTTP block, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow) but the actual product listing/count is fetched client-side via a Coveo search widget. For the first ~7 category pages visited in this session the Coveo widget rendered normally and gave exact 'N PRODUCTS' headers (Dining Tables 374, Dining Chairs 490, Bar & Counter Stools 345, Buffets 284, Dining Benches 60, Coffee Tables 496, Entertainment Units 299 -- all cross-checked by reading the rendered header text twice). Starting with the 8th category (Bar Cabinets & Carts) the widget stopped rendering any product grid, count header, filter or sort control on every subsequent category page -- including re-loading Dining Tables, which had worked minutes earlier -- reproduced across 5 different tabs, 3 of them opened fresh with no prior navigation. This matches the brief's HARD BLOCK RULE ('a page that repeatedly fails to load'): a rate-limit/session block on the Coveo query specifically, not a site-wide access block (SSR/SEO content, breadcrumbs and FAQ blocks kept rendering normally throughout). Per the rule, browser requests to freedom.com.au were stopped rather than chased further. All rows below whose qty is null are furniture nodes whose URL and existence were independently confirmed via the site's own live mega-menu DOM (a full nav dump of <cx-page-slot class=NavigationBar> anchor tags, 424 unique category links site-wide), so the tree/URLs are solid; only their exact qty could not be captured before the block hit.
notes: ACCESS: no Claude/bot-specific Disallow in robots.txt (generic '*' group only, unrelated to category browsing) -- reached entirely via the Claude-in-Chrome connector, no other route used. TREE SOURCE: (1) categorysitemap.xml (234 curated category URLs) fetched via the tab's own DOM (document.querySelectorAll('loc')) after navigating to https://www.freedom.com.au/sitemap.xml -> categorysitemap.xml; (2) the live mega-menu, which is present in full in the DOM under cx-page-slot.NavigationBar even though visually hidden until hover -- dumped via JS (424 unique '/c/' links site-wide), then filtered to furniture-relevant labels; the mega-menu is materially richer than the sitemap (e.g. surfaces the current 'All Sofas / All Armchairs / All Recliners / ...' type-based sofa taxonomy that supersedes the older sitemap-only Fabric/Leather split). QTY METHOD: rendered listing header text 'N PRODUCTS' immediately under the Filter/Sort bar (§4 Rule 1) -- this is the only count source on this platform; no usable structured JSON (the SSR-embedded 'cx-state' script only holds CMS/page metadata, not Coveo search results) and no working public API were found (consistent with the prior Home-Decor pass's finding that even a valid OCC bearer token hit a dead '/greenlitrest/v2/' endpoint). SANITY CHECK: Dining Tables was read twice, ~15 minutes apart, both times before the block, and returned 374 both times. EXCLUSIONS: (a) Fabric Sofas / Leather Sofas and every Fabric-* / Leather-* sibling (Chaises, Sofa Beds, Recliners, Armchairs, Ottomans) -- dropped as material-filtered re-cuts of the All-Sofas/All-Armchairs/All-Recliners/etc. type taxonomy (brief §3: never extract price/colour/material filter pages); both schemes coexist live in the mega-menu, so All-X was kept as the primary type-based breakdown and the material split was treated as a facet re-cut of the same products. (b) Sofa Ranges/All Sofa Ranges, Quick Ship Sofas, Best Selling *, In Stock *, Online Only Sofas, Shop Online Exclusive Sofas/marketplace-all-sofas-and-armchairs, and every Clearance/Sale node -- merchandising/marketing collections per §3. (c) Furniture Protection, Sofa Protection -- furniture care/parts. (d) Baskets, Laundry Hampers, Shoe Racks, Coat Hangers & Wall Hooks, Wardrobe Organisation, Jewellery Organisation, Kitchen Storage, the 'Organisation' grouping, Office Accessories -- standalone storage/accessory products, not furniture. (e) Pet Beds, Pet Sofas, Chair Pads -- not home furniture. (f) All Outdoor Furniture (/c/outdoor) and All Storage (/c/storage) -- broad rollups whose children are already captured individually; kept as un-recorded parents rather than leaves since they have extractable children. (g) Kids Storage Furniture and Kids Organisation Furniture were KEPT (not excluded) -- their SEO copy names wardrobes/storage cabinets/ottomans as the popular types, consistent with genuine kids furniture rather than toy bins; flagged for manual product-level re-check once qty is recoverable. TOP-UP GUIDANCE for whoever revisits: re-open each null-qty URL below (all confirmed live, canonical, English) and read the '.search-result-plp' text / page 'N PRODUCTS' header; pace at least 10-15s apart and stop again immediately if the grid fails to render twice in a row.
